IRS990.MissionDesc: The mission of the Spreckels Organ Society is to preserve, program and promote the Spreckels Organ as a world treasure for all people. The Spreckels Organ Society presents over 65 concerts each year free of charge and open to the public. We also provide scholarships for young organ students and educational programs for children, focusing on Title I schools.
IRS990.Desc: The largest special program expense in 2024 was incurred in order to present the annual San Diego International Summer Organ Festival, featuring top national and international organists. The festival comprised twelve concerts held on Monday evenings from June 17 through September 2. The programs included a special Violin and Organ concert with San Diego Symphony Concertmaster Jeff Thayer and orchestra, a jazz concert, an accompanied silent movie and concerts featuring opera, classic rock and popular music. The Spreckels Organ Society paid for the artists' fees, hotel accommodations and other production costs. There is never an admission charge for our concerts.

ProgSrvcAccomActy2Grp.Desc: The primary programmatic function of the Spreckels Organ Society is providing Sunday and special concerts at the Spreckels Organ Pavilion on our world-famous organ. This is done in coordination with the City of San Diego Parks and Recreation Department. The city pays the civic organist to perform on Sundays, but the Spreckels Organ Society pays the bulk of the organist's compensation. We also pay for extra expenses such as hand programs, additional musicians, vocalists and holiday decorations. The Spreckels Organ Society also provides additional events and concerts throughout the year. In addition to the San Diego International Summer Organ Festival, the Spreckels Organ Society presented several special concerts on Saturdays and holidays during 2024, including Halloween, December Nights and Mother's Day concerts. The Spreckels Organ Society also pays for the organ curator for special concerts.

ProgSrvcAccomActy3Grp.Desc: The Spreckels Organ Society third program is scholarships for organ students. Each year, the San Diego chapter of the American Guild of Organists holds a competition for young organ students, and the Spreckels Organ Society awards scholarships to the top three contestants. The 2024 scholarship winners were Isabella, age 6; Yuhan, age 11 and Aska, age 14.

ProgSrvcAccomActyOtherGrp.Desc: For many years, the Spreckels Organ Society has presented a special program for students, focusing on Title I schools. It includes a demonstration of how the organ works and a mini concert. In 2024, we received a grant to purchase an Orgelkids pipe organ kit, which is a small scale, fully functional organ that teaches valuable STEAM skills while children build the organ in a small group. The goal of the education program is to provide high-quality, accessible music exposure programs for San Diego youth, fostering creative expression, confidence and academic success.

SupplementalInformationDetail.ExplanationTxt: There are four endowment funds. The Evenson Fund was a bequest from the founder of the Spreckels Organ Society, which the board designated as an endowment to be used for maintenance of the organ and for compensation of the artistic director. The Nichols Fund was a bequest that the board designated as an endowment to be used for expenses of the San Diego International Summer Organ Festival. The Operating Expense Endowment Fund was designated by the board as an endowment fund to be used for general expenses. The Lynn Reaser Artistic Director Endowment Fund was created in 2021 when the late Dr. Lynn Reaser made a genenerous donation and agreed to match further donations. She specified that the fund was to be used for the artistic director's compensation.
